{
  "overall_verdict": "ACCEPT_WITH_MINOR_REVISIONS. Relative to the stated premises I(1), G and C, Lemma M is correct, both in the monic version and in the positive-leading nonmonic version, and so is the monic equivalence corollary. No mathematical gap was found in the epsilon*(1+s^n) perturbation, the uniformity at t=0 and t->infinity, or the exact-degree claim. The required repairs are all statement-level: make K subset K0 explicit in the monic statement, state the nonmonic hypotheses precisely, and define the conjecture and the radial boundary class used in the corollary. Novelty is not assessed.",
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "F1-INTERIOR-STRICTNESS",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "M correctly derives that P_{a,beta}(t) > 0 on K x (0,infinity), uniformly on compact t-intervals, and uses I(1) only within its hypotheses.",
      "reason": "Interiority: for a in K and all t>=0, E^0_max(t)-E_a(t) >= u^0_0-a_0 > 0 and E_a(t)-E^0_min(t) >= a_0-l^0_0 > 0. Every other even-index term is a nonnegative multiple of t^l, and the monic top term cancels. The same holds for O via a_1. So (E_a(t),O_a(t)) is interior to K0's rectangle, and that rectangle is exactly the image of K0 because even and odd coefficients vary independently. Nonzero functional: for t>0, (E_beta(t), t*O_beta(t)) = (0,0) iff beta(i*sqrt t) = 0. Use of I(1): it is applied only to L, which is compact, robustly Hurwitz, monic, and has positive constant and linear widths. beta is weak on L because L subset K0. The marginal box K0 is never fed to I(1). Conclusion: a nonzero linear functional that is nonnegative on a rectangle is strictly positive at interior points. Continuity on the compact set K x [r,R], with r>0, then gives delta>0. Only the 'no nonzero imaginary-axis zero' part of I(1) is used.",
      "repair": "None required. Optionally add the one-line interiority inequality and note that it holds for all t>=0."
    },
    {
      "id": "F2-PERTURBATION",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "The epsilon*(1+s^n) perturbation is valid: the quantifier order is correct and a single epsilon works for the whole family K.",
      "reason": "Tail bounds: r and R depend only on K and v. For n=2m, P_{a,v} = E_a(t)(1+(-1)^m t^m). For n=2m+1, P_{a,v} = E_a(t)+(-1)^m t^(m+1) O_a(t). Both have constant term a_0 >= min_K a_0 > 0 and leading coefficient [s^n]a, and all coefficients are bounded by some M on compact K. Hence r = min_K a_0/(2nM) and R = max(1, 2nM/min_K [s^n]a) work, with r<1<=R. Middle interval: P_{a,v} is genuinely indefinite there; for n = 2 mod 4 it vanishes at t=1 for every a. The proof correctly uses only |P_{a,v}| <= C on that interval. delta and C are computed on compact K x [r,R] after r and R are fixed, and epsilon < delta/(1+C) gives epsilon*C < delta, so there is no circularity. Pointwise check: on the middle interval the sum is >= delta - epsilon*C > 0. On the tails it is P_{a,beta} >= 0 (from K subset K0, all t>=0) plus epsilon*P_{a,v} > 0. Only v_0>0 and v_n>0 are used.",
      "repair": "None required. Optionally record explicit r and R, and note that any real v with v_0>0 and v_n>0 works."
    },
    {
      "id": "F3-ENDPOINTS-AND-DEGREE",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "The uniformity at t=0 and t->infinity and the exact-degree claim are correct. Both degenerate cases, beta(0)=0 and deg beta=n-1, are covered.",
      "reason": "At t=0: P_{a,b}(0) = a_0(beta_0+epsilon), and weak pairing at t=0 gives a_0*beta_0 >= 0, so beta_0 >= 0. A simple zero of beta at the origin is therefore absorbed. At infinity: the t^n coefficient of P_{a,beta} is [s^n]a*[s^n]beta, so weak pairing for large t gives [s^n]beta >= 0 directly, without I(1). Hence [s^n]b = [s^n]beta+epsilon > 0, deg b = n exactly, and P_{a,b}(t)/t^n -> [s^n]a*[s^n]b uniformly on K. Consequence for SPR: Re(b/a)(i*omega) is positive on R and tends to [s^n]b/[s^n]a >= [s^n]b/max_K [s^n]a > 0. Even a definition requiring a uniform margin over K x (R union {infinity}) is met. b is automatically Hurwitz by the minimum principle. The I(1) conclusion deg beta in {n-1,n} is never needed by M.",
      "repair": "None required. Optionally remark that b is Hurwitz and that the margin is uniform over K."
    },
    {
      "id": "F4-MONIC-CONTAINMENT",
      "severity": "minor",
      "statement": "The monic statement of M does not explicitly require K subset K0, i.e. that K0 be monic or that its leading interval contain 1.",
      "reason": "'Strictly inside in all n lower coefficient coordinates' says nothing about coordinate n, and K0 is introduced only as 'a coefficient box'. The proof needs K subset K0 in three places: (1) L subset K0, so that beta is weak on L and I(1) applies; (2) interiority of (E_a(t),O_a(t)) in K0's rectangle for large t, which needs the top-degree terms to cancel; (3) P_{a,beta} >= 0 on K at the tails. If K0's leading interval excludes 1, none of these steps is justified. In the corollary K0 is monic, so that application is unaffected.",
      "repair": "Add 'K subset K0' (or 'K0 monic') to the monic hypothesis, matching the nonmonic sentence."
    },
    {
      "id": "F5-HYPOTHESIS-SLACK",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "The strict-interiority hypothesis is stronger than the proof uses.",
      "reason": "The proof uses only strict interiority in the constant and linear coordinates, plus K subset K0. The enlargement to L is needed only in a_0 and a_1, and interiority of the rectangle point comes from the l=0 terms of E and O. Interiority in a_2..a_{n-1} is never used.",
      "repair": "Optional: weaken the hypothesis. It is harmless as stated, and the corollary's K0 satisfies the stronger form anyway."
    },
    {
      "id": "F6-NONMONIC-SCOPE",
      "severity": "minor",
      "statement": "The nonmonic extension of M is correct but should be stated as a separate remark with explicit hypotheses. The corollary does not extend to nonmonic boxes.",
      "reason": "Assume K is compact and robustly Hurwitz, min_K [s^n]a > 0, K subset K0, and the lower coefficients are strictly interior. Then every step goes through. L comes from enlarging only lower coefficients: Hurwitz degree-n polynomials with nonzero leading coefficient form an open set, so compactness gives a margin. I(1) is stated for positive-leading boxes. Interiority uses only a_0 and a_1. P_{a,v} has leading coefficient [s^n]a >= min_K [s^n]a > 0; the text's 'bounded uniformly away from zero' must be read with the positive sign. [s^n]beta >= 0 follows from weak pairing with a in L. K0 need not be stable or positive-leading. The corollary is a different matter: G's radial construction, the conjecture, and necessity C are all monic, and dividing by the leading coefficient does not preserve box structure. A nonmonic radial construction would have to say whether the leading interval is scaled; if it is, the first boundary could be a degree drop rather than an imaginary-axis root.",
      "repair": "State nonmonic M with explicit hypotheses: compact, robustly Hurwitz, min_K [s^n]a > 0, K subset K0, strictness at least in a_0 and a_1. Keep the corollary explicitly monic-only and claim no nonmonic equivalence."
    },
    {
      "id": "F7-COROLLARY-DEFINITIONS",
      "severity": "minor",
      "statement": "The corollary's equivalence is correct, but neither side is restated, and G's 'all widths positive' wording conflicts with the monic setting.",
      "reason": "Define the two sides. Conj_n: every compact robustly Hurwitz monic degree-n box K has b with deg b = n and P_{a,b}(t) > 0 for all a in K and t>=0. B_n: the set of K0 = c+lambda*(c,r)[-r,r] over monic centers c and radii with r_i > 0 (i<n) and r_n = 0 such that c+[-r,r] is robustly Hurwitz. Necessity (C), verified: as lambda increases to lambda*, the shrunken boxes are stable and have exact-degree numerators b_lambda. Normalized limits give a nonzero beta of degree <= n. For a in K0, the points c+(lambda/lambda*)(a-c) lie in the shrunken boxes and converge to a, so P_{a,beta} >= 0 on K0 x [0,infinity). Sufficiency, verified: G gives K strictly inside K', and K' subset K0 in B_n, with l^0_i = c_i - lambda* r_i < l'_i < l_i because lambda* > 1. So M applies. Wording: 'all widths positive' in G must mean the n lower widths, since the monic leading width is 0.",
      "repair": "Restate the corollary as: for each n>=3, Conj_n holds iff every K0 in B_n admits a nonzero beta of degree <= n with P_{a,beta} >= 0 on K0 x [0,infinity). State that G enlarges only the lower coefficients."
    },
    {
      "id": "F8-NO-EXISTENCE",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "The corollary is a reformulation, not progress on existence. The authors' disclaimer is accurate and must stay.",
      "reason": "The equivalent condition concerns boxes K0 that are not robustly Hurwitz; each contains a polynomial with an imaginary-axis root. So I(1) cannot be applied to K0 to produce or constrain beta, and the quantifier still ranges over all radial boundary strata. Sufficiency needs only one K0 per K, but necessity supplies all of B_n, so the equivalence is unchanged.",
      "repair": "None. Keep the disclaimer and avoid any wording that suggests synthesis is established."
    },
    {
      "id": "F9-CONDITIONALITY",
      "severity": "info",
      "statement": "The phrase 'without a zero-free premise' is accurate only in the sense that zero-freeness away from the origin is derived from I(1). M remains conditional on I(1), and the corollary on I(1), G and C.",
      "reason": "The only nonelementary input is I(1)'s exclusion of nonzero imaginary-axis zeros for weak numerators of a strictly stable box with positive constant and linear widths. This review did not re-audit I(1), G or C. It only checked that hypotheses match and checked the short compactness argument in C.",
      "repair": "Label M 'conditional on I(1)' and the corollary 'conditional on I(1), G, C'. The '[proved here]' tag must not be read as a novelty claim, and this review makes none."
    }
  ],
  "theorem_verdict": "Lemma M (monic): CORRECT conditional on I(1), once the hypothesis K subset K0 is made explicit (F4). Lemma M (positive-leading nonmonic): CORRECT when K is compact and robustly Hurwitz, min_K [s^n]a > 0, K subset K0, and the lower coefficients are strictly interior. The numerator beta+epsilon(1+s^n) has exact degree n and strictly positive pairing on K x [0,infinity) with a uniform margin; beta(0)=0 and deg beta=n-1 are both handled. Corollary: CORRECT for each fixed n>=3 in the monic case, conditional on I(1), G and C. It is an equivalence between Conj_n and the existence of a nonzero weak numerator on every radial first-stability-boundary box. It proves no existence and has no nonmonic version.",
  "original_problem_scope": "This material does NOT resolve the original monic robust SPR synthesis question: whether, for n>=3, every compact robustly Hurwitz monic degree-n interval box admits a common SPR numerator of exact degree n. M and the corollary show only that, conditional on I(1), G and C, the question is equivalent for each n>=3 to the existence of a nonzero weak (closed) numerator on every radial first-stability-boundary box, including degenerate boundary strata. I(1) is unavailable on those boxes because they are not robustly Hurwitz. This review claims no full synthesis theorem, no existence of boundary numerators, no nonmonic equivalence, and no novelty."
}
```
